content.user_title: Ship Changes Through Pull Requests and CI
content.value_statement: Finishing a change requires careful verification, commits, pull-request setup, and CI follow-through. This skill manages that workflow until every check passes.
actual_capabilities: Finds repository-specific build, formatting, linting, and test commands before committing.
Inspects the working tree and stages explicit paths for focused commits.
Creates or updates a ready pull request with verification details.
Watches every CI check and reads failed job logs.
Fixes CI failures, reruns local checks, commits corrections, and pushes updates.
Reports the pull-request link, shipped commits, and final CI status.
limitations: Requires Git, repository access, and authenticated GitHub CLI access.
Cannot complete checks that require unavailable tools, services, platforms, or approvals.
Relies on repository documentation and CI configuration to identify the correct checks.
Changes commits and remote pull-request state, so users should review the working tree first.

use_cases.title: Finish a feature branch
use_cases.description: Verify completed work, create logical commits, open a ready pull request, and monitor CI.

use_cases.title: Resolve pull-request failures
use_cases.description: Inspect failed CI logs, correct the implementation, rerun local gates, and push a focused fix.

use_cases.title: Standardize delivery evidence
use_cases.description: Produce consistent commit messages, pull-request context, testing records, and a final green-status report.

prompt_templates.title: Ship completed work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $ship-it to verify the current changes, commit them, open a ready pull request, and wait for all CI checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has finished a small change on a feature branch.

prompt_templates.title: Ship with focused verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $ship-it for this branch. Run the repository checks that cover the changed modules, then create the pull request and resolve CI failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants checks selected from repository guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $ship-it to reuse the open pull request for this branch. Refresh its details, mark it ready, and drive every check to green.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer has an existing draft or outdated pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Ship a complex issue fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $ship-it to inspect the full diff and split related changes into logical commits. Link the issue, document exact tests, and resolve the complete CI matrix.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced contributor needs a traceable multi-commit delivery.

output_examples.input: Ship the completed cache fix and reference issue 142.
output_examples.output: Opened a ready pull request for issue 142. Unit tests, linting, formatting, and the full CI matrix passed.

output_examples.input: Get the current pull request green after the integration test failed.
output: Reviewed the complete failed-job log and corrected the stale fixture.
Reran the relevant local tests and pushed one focused fix commit.

output_examples.input: Commit these documentation updates and open a pull request.
output_examples.output: Created a focused documentation commit and opened a ready pull request with the validation results. All required checks passed.

best_practices: Review the complete diff and preserve unrelated user changes before invoking the workflow.
Keep repository documentation and CI configuration accurate so local verification matches required checks.
Confirm GitHub authentication and branch protections before starting a workflow that may require approval.
anti_patterns: Do not invoke the skill on the default branch when the repository requires feature branches.
Do not treat skipped integration tests as successful coverage without checking required services.
Do not stop after one passing job when other matrix jobs or required checks remain.

faq.question: Does this skill push changes automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. Invoking the skill authorizes committing, pushing the feature branch, and creating or updating its pull request.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. It finds the pull request for the current branch, updates its details, and marks a draft ready when needed.

faq.question: How does it choose local checks?
faq.answer: It reads contributor documentation and CI configuration, then runs the relevant formatter, linter, build, and tests.

faq.question: What happens when CI fails?
faq.answer: It reads the failed-job log, diagnoses the cause, fixes the change, reruns local gates, commits, pushes, and watches CI again.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI access?
faq.answer: Yes. Pull-request creation, updates, status monitoring, and CI log access require an authenticated GitHub CLI session.

faq.question: When does the workflow pause?
faq.answer: It pauses for material ambiguity, required approval, missing access, or a failure that cannot be resolved with available tools.
